summary.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore despite 19% higher gross income, as feed raw-material costs squeezed margins.
summary.overview: Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore but PBT fell 15% QoQ to INR 157 crore and 37% YoY. The Feed division's gross income rose 27% YoY to INR 1,615 crore on 28,287 MT higher volume, yet PBT dropped 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices surged. Feed PBT margin fell to 7.06% from about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26. Shrimp Processing and Export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations and forex. Management took a roughly 10% feed price hike in June 2026 and said industry and government are working on a raw-material price mechanism.

segments.name: Shrimp Feed (standalone Feed division)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 1,615 crore and PBT INR 114 crore on 1,93,852 MT of sales; PBT hit by higher fish meal (INR 153/kg avg vs INR 123 in Q4 and INR 93 in Q1 FY26) and soya bean meal (INR 58/kg vs INR 49 and INR 40).

segments.name: Shrimp Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 350 crore, down 22% QoQ and 7% YoY on 15-16% lower volume; PBT INR 45 crore helped by better selling prices, favourable forex and higher other income. Realisations fell in Q4 after reciprocal tariffs were withdrawn from 24 February 2026.

segments.name: Pet food (Avant Furst, Avanti PetCare)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 180 lakh in Q1 FY27 vs INR 151 lakh in Q4 FY26; distribution in Tier 1 cities expanding to Tier 2/3, available on Amazon and Supertail. Land purchased near Hyderabad for a plant, about INR 25 crore spent of an estimated INR 175 crore.

guidance_outlook: Company feed sales estimated at about 5,85,000 MT in FY27, against 5,62,060 MT in FY26; analyst noted this implies roughly 5-6% annualised growth.
Shrimp exports estimated at about 19,000 MT in FY27, against 16,976 MT in FY26.
Management expects raw-material prices to stabilise in coming months as fresh crops arrive and monsoon eases El Nino effects, but called FY27 a challenging season for aquaculture.
On the Q2 question, management agreed that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the benefit of the price hike and any government intervention plays out.
Shrimp production estimated at 8-9 lakh MT in calendar 2026, with feed consumption estimated at 11-12 lakh MT.
capex_capacity: Pet food plant: land near Hyderabad converted to non-agricultural use; Consent for Establishment application filed and approval pending, construction to start after approval.
Pet food capex estimated at about INR 175 crore in total, of which about INR 25 crore spent on land so far.
No feed capacity, utilisation or new feed plant commentary was given in the call.
demand_pricing: Farm activity described as good: favourable climate and farmers reporting strong culture progress through the second season to December 2026. Management said cost is the only concern.
Feed price hike of around 10% taken on 19 June 2026, effective about 10 July 2026 (speaker's dates were unclear in the transcript).

Government of Andhra Pradesh has formed a committee with a big-four consultant to design a feed price mechanism linked to fish meal, soya bean meal and wheat flour; management said further hikes need affordability balance for farmers.
Wheat flour price fell to INR 28/kg in Q1 FY27 from INR 31/kg; current spot prices are fish meal INR 225/kg, soya bean meal INR 71/kg, wheat flour INR 33/kg.
Frozen shrimp exports FY26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA 33% share, China 21%, EU 17%. US volumes fell 17.9% YoY; China rose 24%, EU 36%, Japan 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Khanna (Kotak MF) asked how farm-gate shrimp prices are trending given global protein inflation and rupee depreciation, and why shrimp prices have not moved up like other proteins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said farm-gate prices balance global prices against processor/exporter economics and farmer affordability, and are fixed from time to time. It gave no specific reason for the lack of upward move; prices move with domestic availability and global demand.

qa_highlights.question: Khanna asked whether further feed price hikes are envisaged given rising input costs and margin pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said any hike requires balancing farmer affordability and feed-industry sustainability, with the Andhra Pradesh government having a say. A government-formed committee with a big-four consultant is working on the pricing approach, and no further hike was committed.

qa_highlights.question: Khanna asked for an update on the US reciprocal tariff refund, where USD 15-20 million had earlier been mentioned.
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said refunds are stuck because the ADD/CVD review entries are under suspension and CBP will not process reciprocal tariff refunds until that is lifted. The company has declared the entries as its legal counsel and customs broker advised.

qa_highlights.question: Ronak Shah (Equirus) asked how farmers view current shrimp activity, given the 17% YoY feed volume growth and the 5-6% annualised growth implied by the FY27 target of 5.85 lakh MT.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shrimp culture is going well with favourable climate and good culture progress, with farm-gate prices up. The only concern is feed cost, and it hopes for raw-material price stabilisation in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked whether a price hike was taken in the last three to four months, whether more is planned, and whether formulation changes are being evaluated to mitigate ingredient volatility.
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a price hike of around 10%, taken on 19 June 2026 and effective around 10 July. It is also working on formulation and quality to reduce raw-material usage without compromising feed quality or FCR.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked for confirmation that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the price hike and government intervention play out.
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the summary, answering yes.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked about the pet food capex cycle and investment to date.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR 175 crore total pet food investment, with about INR 25 crore spent so far on land.

risks_watch: Feed margin compression: Feed PBT margin at 7.06% vs about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26, with management conceding Q2 may be another weak quarter.
Price hike of around 10% (June 2026) may not offset raw-material costs; further hikes are subject to Andhra Pradesh government committee outcome and farmer affordability.
US reciprocal tariff refund (USD 15-20 million previously mentioned) on hold until ADD/CVD review suspension is lifted; timing unclear.
Shrimp export volumes: US volumes down 17.9% YoY in FY26 and FY27 export target of about 19,000 MT vs 16,976 MT; realisations hit after reciprocal tariffs were withdrawn from 24 February 2026.
Pet food capex of about INR 175 crore pending Consent for Establishment approval for the Hyderabad plant; construction timing depends on approval.

Monitor next quarter: fish meal and soya bean meal price trend (spot INR 225/kg and INR 71/kg), feed volumes against the 5.85 lakh MT FY27 target, and whether the Shrimp Processing segment sustains its PBT of INR 45 crore.
key_quotes: The PBT during the quarter stood at 7.06% on revenue as compared to about 13% during Q4 FY 26 and 17% during Q1 FY26.
The government has, in fact, constituted a committee with one of the big four consultants.
We are estimating around INR 175 crores investment in a pet food.
summary.management_tone: Management was defensive and cautious on the feed margin squeeze, repeatedly stressing affordability for farmers and the need for a government-led price mechanism rather than committing to further hikes. It was more confident on farm activity and volumes, and it was vague or deferred on the US tariff refund and on farm-gate price direction.
